bugs.summary: methods:::.identicalGeneric can wrongly ignore differences in default values of formal arguments

comments.text:
Created attachment 3434
methods:::.identicalGeneric comparing default expressions also when names match without "..."

This bug is related to but different from bug 18831.

Currently, the installation output of **Matrix** ends with:

```
** byte-compile and prepare package for lazy loading
Creating a generic function for 'drop' from package 'base' in package 'Matrix'
Creating a generic function for 'chol2inv' from 'base' in package 'Matrix'
    (from the saved implicit definition)
Creating a generic function for 'chol2inv' from package 'base' in package 'Matrix'
## <irrelevant noise due to missing class definitions>
Creating a generic function for 'colSums' from package 'base' in package 'Matrix'
Creating a generic function for 'colMeans' from package 'base' in package 'Matrix'
Creating a generic function for 'rowSums' from package 'base' in package 'Matrix'
Creating a generic function for 'rowMeans' from package 'base' in package 'Matrix'
Creating a generic function for 'cov2cor' from package 'stats' in package 'Matrix'
Creating a generic function for 'diag' from package 'base' in package 'Matrix'
Creating a generic function for 'diag<-' from package 'base' in package 'Matrix'
Creating a generic function for 'norm' from package 'base' in package 'Matrix'
Creating a generic function for 'qr.Q' from package 'base' in package 'Matrix'
Creating a generic function for 'qr.R' from package 'base' in package 'Matrix'
Creating a generic function for 'qr.X' from package 'base' in package 'Matrix'
Creating a generic function for 'qr.coef' from package 'base' in package 'Matrix'
Creating a generic function for 'qr.fitted' from package 'base' in package 'Matrix'
Creating a generic function for 'qr.resid' from package 'base' in package 'Matrix'
Creating a generic function for 'qr.qty' from package 'base' in package 'Matrix'
Creating a generic function for 'qr.qy' from package 'base' in package 'Matrix'
Creating a generic function for 'rcond' from 'base' in package 'Matrix'
    (from the saved implicit definition)
Creating a generic function for 'rcond' from package 'base' in package 'Matrix'
Creating a generic function for 'toeplitz' from 'stats' in package 'Matrix'
    (from the saved implicit definition)
Creating a generic function for 'toeplitz' from package 'stats' in package 'Matrix'
Creating a generic function for 'which' from package 'base' in package 'Matrix'
Creating a generic function for 'zapsmall' from package 'base' in package 'Matrix'
```

The output is from `setMethod` calls in `Matrix/R/*.R`.  What struck me as odd is that `chol2inv`, `rcond`, and `toeplitz` get the parenthetical `(from the saved implicit definition)`, while other functions with implicit generic function definitions, such as `norm` and `qr.X`, do not.

It turns out that `setGeneric(<implicit>)`, which is called from `setMethod(<implicit>)`, uses `methods:::.identicalGeneric` to test whether the signatures of the implicit generic function and "original" function are similar enough.  If the answer is "no", then it signals the message with parenthesis.

It makes sense, then, that the message is signaled for `chol2inv`, `rcond`, and `toeplitz`:

```
> args(rcond)
function (x, norm = c("O", "I", "1"), triangular = FALSE, uplo = "U", 
    ...) 
NULL
> args(methods:::.implicitTable[["rcond"]])
function (x, norm, ...) 
NULL
> setClass("zzz")
> setMethod("rcond", c(x = "zzz", norm = "missing"), function(x, norm, ...) NULL)
Creating a generic function for 'rcond' from 'base' in the global environment
    (from the saved implicit definition)
Creating a generic function for 'rcond' from package 'base' in the global environment
> 
```

The "bug" is that the message is not __also__ signaled for `colSums`, `colMeans`, `rowSums`, `rowMeans`, `norm`, and `qr.X`.  In each of these cases, the formal arguments other than `...` have the identical names but non-identical default expressions.  `methods:::.identicalGeneric` "forgets" to tests for differences in the default expressions.

```
> args(norm)
function (x, type = c("O", "I", "F", "M", "2")) 
NULL
> args(methods:::.implicitTable[["norm"]])
function (x, type, ...) 
NULL
> setClass("zzz")
> setMethod("norm", c(x = "zzz", type = "missing"), function(x, type, ...) NULL)
Creating a generic function for 'norm' from package 'base' in the global environment
> 
```

A small adjustment to logic in `methods:::.identicalGeneric` fixes the bug.

```
Index: src/library/methods/R/Methods.R
===================================================================
--- src/library/methods/R/Methods.R	(revision 87423)
+++ src/library/methods/R/Methods.R	(working copy)
@@ -1473,7 +1473,9 @@
     ## xtra... <- FALSE
     if(!identical(formals(f1d), formals(f2d))) {
 	a1 <- names(formals(f1d)); a2 <- names(formals(f2d))
-	if(identical(a1, a2))
+	if(identical(a1, a2) ||
+	   (identical(c(a1, "..."), a2) && allow.extra.dots &&
+	    !identical(`length<-`(formals(f1d), length(a2)), formals(f2d))))
 	    return(gettext("formal arguments differ (in default values?)"))
 	else if(identical(c(a1, "..."), a2) && allow.extra.dots)
             ## silently accept an extra "..."
```

Now:

```
> setClass("zzz")
> setMethod("norm", c(x = "zzz", type = "missing"), function(x, type, ...) NULL)
Creating a generic function for 'norm' from 'base' in the global environment
    (from the saved implicit definition)
Creating a generic function for 'norm' from package 'base' in the global environment
> 
```

comments.text:
Oops - the patch above mixed up `1` and `2` and so failed in `reg-S4.R`.  The one below passes `make check-all`.

```
Index: src/library/methods/R/Methods.R
===================================================================
--- src/library/methods/R/Methods.R	(revision 87423)
+++ src/library/methods/R/Methods.R	(working copy)
@@ -1473,7 +1473,9 @@
     ## xtra... <- FALSE
     if(!identical(formals(f1d), formals(f2d))) {
 	a1 <- names(formals(f1d)); a2 <- names(formals(f2d))
-	if(identical(a1, a2))
+	if(identical(a1, a2) ||
+	   (identical(c(a1, "..."), a2) && allow.extra.dots &&
+	    !identical(`length<-`(formals(f2d), length(a1)), formals(f1d))))
 	    return(gettext("formal arguments differ (in default values?)"))
 	else if(identical(c(a1, "..."), a2) && allow.extra.dots)
             ## silently accept an extra "..."
```
